correctness.rationale: For fixed C^3 positively curved convex K, the normal map is injective on a sufficiently small shell and its exact Jacobian is (1-kappa u); shell area is P epsilon-pi epsilon^2. Uniform positive curvature localizes visible pairs to boundary arclength difference O(sqrt epsilon). Uniform Taylor expansion of inward signed distance along the joining segment yields A(1-t)+Bt+(kappa z^2/2)t(1-t), with no missing boundary terms. The inequality for every t in [0,1] is equivalent to |z|<=sqrt(2/kappa)(sqrt(1-A)+sqrt(1-B)). Dominated convergence in the bounded scaled separation variable gives coefficient 8 sqrt(2)/(3P^2) integral kappa^(-1/2) ds. Jensen and total curvature 2pi give the unique circle equality. Exact disk formula and independently clipped elliptical shell samples from the packaged Python script passed; finite diagnostics do not prove the general claim.

value.rationale: The exact leading visibility invariant of a Euclidean normal shell quantifies how curvature changes the ability of two uniformly sampled boundary-near points to see each other. It identifies a universal sqrt-thickness law, a nontrivial curvature integral and the sharp fixed-perimeter disk optimizer, rather than merely a zero limit or a circle-specific formula. This is a natural complete first-order asymptotic shape problem; it does not depend on a speculative downstream application.
